result.target_summary: The Board delegates oversight and risk management responsibilities to five standing committees: Audit, Compensation, Nomination, Risk Management, and Technology.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures detail the Board's delegation of oversight and risk management responsibilities to five specific standing committees: Audit, Compensation, Nomination, Risk Management, and Technology.

Both disclosures cover the overarching risk management environment and culture. D168 details the Board's delegation of oversight to committees including the Risk Management Committee which oversees the risk management framework and culture. D125 establishes the ERM Framework and states that Citi's culture drives a strong risk and control environment and is at the heart of the ERM Framework.

current_disclosures.summary: Citi has established an Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework to manage risks appropriately across the company, underpinned by a culture that drives a strong risk and control environment. This framework ensures that business activities remain consistent with Citi's Mission, Value Proposition, Leadership Principles, and risk appetite.

current_disclosures.summary: The Board delegates risk oversight to five standing committees: the Audit Committee (financial controls/compliance), the Compensation, Performance Management and Culture Committee (compensation/culture), the Nomination, Governance and Public Affairs Committee (governance/public affairs), the Risk Management Committee (enterprise risk framework/capital), and the Technology Committee (technology strategy/cybersecurity/GenAI).

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure introduces a new section on the ERM Framework Overview, explicitly stating that Citi's culture drives the risk and control environment and is 'at the heart of the ERM Framework.' It also updates the Technology Committee's charter to specifically mention oversight of 'Generative AI.' These changes reflect a meaningful shift in how the company articulates its risk governance structure and priorities, particularly regarding the integration of culture into the ERM framework and the emerging threat of GenAI.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Introduction of culture-centric ERM framework and GenAI oversight

comparisons.peer_summary: The Audit Committee oversees the qualifications, performance, and independence of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, the corporate audit function, financial statement integrity, legal/regulatory compliance, and NYSE listing standards compliance, including inquiries into audit scope and resource limitations.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and Bank of America (BAC) disclose the specific oversight responsibilities of their Audit Committees regarding financial reporting integrity and regulatory compliance. Citigroup's Audit Committee is responsible for overseeing the integrity of financial statements, internal accounting controls, and compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. Similarly, Bank of America's Audit Committee oversees the integrity of consolidated financial statements and compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, but additionally highlights its responsibility for overseeing compliance risks pursuant to NYSE listing standards and inquiring into scope or resource limitations of the corporate audit function.

sentences.text: • Audit Committee: assists the Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibility relating to (i) the integrity of Citigroup's consolidated financial statements, financial reporting process and systems of internal accounting and financial controls, (ii) the performance of the internal audit function (Internal Audit), (iii) the annual independent integrated audit of Citigroup's consolidated financial statements and effectiveness of Citigroup's internal control over financial reporting, the engagement of the independent registered public accounting firm (Independent Auditors) and the evaluation of the Independent Auditors' qualifications, independence and performance, (iv) holding management accountable for the effectiveness of Citigroup's control environment and status of corrective actions, including the timely remediation of control breaks (including, without limitation, significant compliance or operational control breaks), (v) policy standards and guidelines for risk assessment and risk management, (vi) Citigroup's compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, including Citigroup's disclosure controls and procedures and (vii) the fulfillment of the other responsibilities set out in the Audit Committee's Charter.

The Audit Committee oversees the qualifications, performance and independence of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, the performance of our corporate audit function, the integrity of our consolidated financial statements, our compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, and makes inquiries of senior management or the Chief Audit Executive (CAE) to determine whether there are scope or resource limitations that impede the ability of Corporate Audit to execute its responsibilities.
The Audit Committee is also responsible for overseeing compliance risks pursuant to the New York Stock Exchange listing standards.

comparisons.peer_summary: Internal Audit serves as the third line of defense, reporting to the Audit Committee and CEO, and is responsible for independently assessing and validating the effectiveness of key controls within the risk management framework.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs (GS) describe the role of the Board's Audit Committee in risk governance and internal control oversight. Citigroup delegates authority to its Audit Committee to oversee risk management responsibilities, including policy standards for risk assessment and the status of corrective actions for control breaks. In contrast, GS describes Internal Audit as the 'third line of defense' that reports to the Audit Committee and is responsible for independently assessing and validating the effectiveness of key controls within the risk management framework, providing a specific structural detail about the internal audit function's reporting line and validation duties not explicitly detailed in C's general committee authority description.

sentences.text: The Board has delegated authority to the following Board standing committees to help fulfill its oversight and risk management responsibilities:

• Audit Committee: assists the Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibility relating to (i) the integrity of Citigroup's consolidated financial statements, financial reporting process and systems of internal accounting and financial controls, (ii) the performance of the internal audit function (Internal Audit), (iii) the annual independent integrated audit of Citigroup's consolidated financial statements and effectiveness of Citigroup's internal control over financial reporting, the engagement of the independent registered public accounting firm (Independent Auditors) and the evaluation of the Independent Auditors' qualifications, independence and performance, (iv) holding management accountable for the effectiveness of Citigroup's control environment and status of corrective actions, including the timely remediation of control breaks (including, without limitation, significant compliance or operational control breaks), (v) policy standards and guidelines for risk assessment and risk management, (vi) Citigroup's compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, including Citigroup's disclosure controls and procedures and (vii) the fulfillment of the other responsibilities set out in the Audit Committee's Charter.
Internal Audit is considered our third line of defense, and our director of Internal Audit reports to the Audit Committee of the Board and administratively to our chief executive officer.

Internal Audit is responsible for independently assessing and validating the effectiveness of key controls, including those within the risk management framework, and providing timely reporting to the Audit Committee of the Board, senior management and regulators.

comparisons.peer_topic: JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. board oversight
comparisons.peer_summary: The JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. Board of Directors oversees management of the bank, with risk, control, and compensation oversight delegated to specific Firm Board committees.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase disclose the delegation of Board oversight responsibilities to standing committees, specifically regarding risk and control. Citigroup's Board delegates authority to standing committees including the Audit Committee to fulfill oversight and risk management responsibilities, with specific attention to control environments and corrective actions. JPMorgan Chase's Board of Directors for JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. discharges oversight through principal standing committees, explicitly delegating risk oversight to the Board Risk Committee and control/audit matters to the Audit Committee.

sentences.text: The Board has delegated authority to the following Board standing committees to help fulfill its oversight and risk management responsibilities:

The JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. Board of Directors is responsible for the oversight of management of the bank, which it discharges both acting directly and through the principal standing committees of the Firm's Board of Directors.

Risk and control oversight on behalf of JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. is primarily the responsibility of the Board Risk Committee and the Audit Committee, respectively, and, with respect to compensation and other management-related matters, the Compensation & Management Development Committee.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Audit Committee of the Board (BAC) oversees the integrity of financial statements, legal/regulatory compliance, internal controls, and risk management guidelines, while also appointing and monitoring the independent auditor and Chief Audit Officer.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley (MS) detail the comprehensive oversight responsibilities of their Audit Committees concerning financial integrity, compliance, and risk management. Citigroup's Audit Committee oversees financial statement integrity, internal controls, compliance with legal requirements, and risk assessment policies. Morgan Stanley's Audit Committee similarly oversees financial statement integrity, legal/regulatory compliance, internal controls, and risk management guidelines, while also explicitly mentioning the appointment and oversight of the independent auditor and the review of major legal and compliance risk exposures.

sentences.text: • Audit Committee: assists the Board in fulfilling its oversight responsibility relating to (i) the integrity of Citigroup's consolidated financial statements, financial reporting process and systems of internal accounting and financial controls, (ii) the performance of the internal audit function (Internal Audit), (iii) the annual independent integrated audit of Citigroup's consolidated financial statements and effectiveness of Citigroup's internal control over financial reporting, the engagement of the independent registered public accounting firm (Independent Auditors) and the evaluation of the Independent Auditors' qualifications, independence and performance, (iv) holding management accountable for the effectiveness of Citigroup's control environment and status of corrective actions, including the timely remediation of control breaks (including, without limitation, significant compliance or operational control breaks), (v) policy standards and guidelines for risk assessment and risk management, (vi) Citigroup's compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, including Citigroup's disclosure controls and procedures and (vii) the fulfillment of the other responsibilities set out in the Audit Committee's Charter.

The Audit Committee of the Board ("BAC") oversees the integrity of our financial statements, compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, and system of internal controls; oversees risk management and risk assessment guidelines in coordination with the Board and other Board committees; reviews the major legal, compliance and financial crime risk exposures of the Firm and the steps management has taken to monitor and control such exposures; appoints, compensates, retains, oversees, evaluates and, when appropriate, replaces the independent auditor; oversees the qualifications, performance and independence of our independent auditor and pre-approves audit and permitted non-audit services; oversees the performance of our Chief Audit Officer; and, after review, recommends to the Board the acceptance and inclusion of the annual audited financial statements in the Firm's annual report on Form 10-K.
